reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) directly demonstrates fast segregation of Cr, Mn, Ni to grain boundaries in CrMnFeCoNi HEA at intermediate temperatures, links it to ductility loss, and shows that preexisting Cr-rich precipitates mitigate this embrittlement by absorbing the segregating elements, with experimental validation at 600–700°C. All key premises are accurately represented and well-supported.
premises: Deformation at intermediate T and high strain rate induces fast nanosegregation of principal elements (Ni, Cr, Mn) to grain boundaries in single-phase HEA
This segregation reduces grain-boundary cohesion and causes a ductile-to-brittle transition
Preexisting grain-boundary precipitates (e.g., Cr-rich σ phase) can absorb the segregating elements
Absorption by precipitates suppresses brittle intergranular fracture and preserves toughness
